title: Adhesion-certainty in faith greater than in any science
source_text: XXXIX. Unde oritur in fide major quaedam certitudo quam sit in ulla scientia. Siquidem mens fidelis sic affecta atque disposita Dei verbum, & quae fidei sunt, avidius suscipit, arctius amplectitur, & firmius retinet: quam quidlibet aliud sub quovis tandem lumine proponatur, & quocunque demonstrationum robore confirmetur. Atque adeo vir vera fide imbutus mente animoque fixum & ratum habet omnibus aliis potius scientiis renunciare quam fidem abjicere. Nec est ulla cognitio quam ita firmiter atque studiose custodiat & retineat; Neque ullus assensus, quem aegrius & difficilius a mente sibi revelli patiatur.
pass_a_gloss: Whence there arises in faith a certain greater certainty than there is in any science. Seeing that the faithful mind so affected and disposed receives God’s word and the things of faith more eagerly, embraces them more closely, and retains them more firmly than anything else proposed under whatever light and confirmed by whatever strength of demonstrations. And so a man imbued with true faith has it fixed and ratified in mind and soul rather to renounce all other sciences than to cast off faith. Nor is there any cognition which he so firmly and studiously guards and retains; nor any assent which he would more grudgingly and hardly suffer to be torn from his mind.
pass_b_english: Eagerer receive, closer embrace, firmer retain than any demonstrated light.
Rather renounce all sciences than cast off faith; hardest assent to tear away.
